content:
The image shows a split soybean stem/root being held in hand. Key observations:
- Stem split lengthwise revealing internal tissue
- Pith appears **brown/tan discolored** (not white)
- The internal vascular/pith tissue shows clear browning throughout
- External stem appears somewhat bleached/gray
- Dead plant at harvest stage, field in background

This internal browning of pith and vascular tissue when the stem is split is the hallmark diagnostic feature of **Brown Stem Rot**. The description states: "when stems are split lengthwise, browning of pith and vascular tissue is evident especially at nodes and in the lower stem; healthy stems have white pith, while BSR-infected stems have brown pith."

Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS) would show **white pith** when split — this stem clearly has brown pith. White Mold would show fluffy white mycelium and black sclerotia. Neither fits.

Healthy stems have white pith; this stem has distinctly brown pith. SDS is ruled out because SDS shows white pith when split. No white mycelium or sclerotia to suggest White Mold."}
